- Each generated image is a single thin (about 1 pixel) white circle outline, a ring, on a black background.
- The ring always lies inside rows and columns 1–10, and the outermost frame stays black.
- The radius varies from small (about 2 pixels, diameter about 4–5) up to large (about 4.5 pixels, diameter 10, touching rows 1 and 10 and columns 1 and 10).

- Each image is a single solid white disk (filled circle) on a black background.
- The diameter ranges from about 4 px up to about 9–10 px.
- The disk sits at a varying position, always fully inside the inner 10×10 area. The outermost 1-pixel frame stays black.
- The largest disks are nearly the inscribed circle, touching rows 1 and 10 and columns 1 and 10, but never reaching the corners.

One white, 1-pixel-thick rectangle outline per image, on black. Its sides lie anywhere from row/column 1 to row/column 10. Sizes range from small boxes (about 4×4) up to nearly the full 10×10 interior. The inside of the box is black, and the outermost border of the image stays black.

Each image is a single solid white axis-aligned rectangle (sometimes a square) on a black background. It sits inside the 1-pixel black frame, with sides typically 4 to 10 pixels long. Its position and width/height vary independently, so it can be placed off-centre. Most rectangles are fairly large and cover much of the central region.

Each image is one solid white, axis-aligned filled rectangle on a black background. It always lies inside the central 10×10 area (rows 1–10, columns 1–10), and the 1-pixel outer frame is always black. Position, width and height vary independently. Sizes run from thin bars of 1–2 px up to nearly the whole 10×10 area; typically a side is about 3–8 px, roughly a quarter to a half of the canvas.

A thin white triangle outline on a black background, pointing up.
- The apex is near the top centre (row 1, columns about 5–6).
- Two one-pixel legs slope down to the left and right.
- A horizontal base sits around rows 7–10 and spans up to about columns 1–10.
- The outer border stays black. Size and slopes vary: some triangles are tall and wide, others shorter and narrower.

Each image is a single solid white triangle pointing upward on a black background:
- The apex is near the top centre, around row 1–2 and columns 5–6.
- The sides slope outward by about one column every two rows.
- The flat base sits around rows 8–10 and spans roughly columns 1–10.
- The triangle is typically about 8–9 pixels tall and 8–10 pixels wide.
